label: Modal spine A3′: pricing the endless-past and never-generated horns of the initial-state view
summary: Target: the two horns left to the initial-state view by ContingentComingToBe.possibleContingentFreePast (attempt 59ac4727): in every accessible history either (H1) some contingent concrete thing was never preceded by its own absence, or (H2) no moment with a contingent concrete thing present has a founded past. Specs: specs/modal-spine-coming-to-be-horns.toml. H2 replacement account: a beginningless succession in which each contingent thing comes to be and is preceded, and even grounded, by an earlier one (control 3: integer time, each individual grounded by its predecessor). H2 findings. (a) Grim Reaper: under the Reaper assembly bridge (an endless descent below a populated moment of an accessible history would admit a Nat-indexed station system obeying the four local rules of IndexedSignalReaper), every populated moment of every accessible history has a founded past (populatedPastsFoundedOfReaper: dependent choice extracts the descent, the composed IndexedSignalReaper.impossible refutes the stations). The bridge is causal (stations respond to signals) and, given that verified impossibility, exactly as strong as its conclusion: the result locates H2's price at the assembly/patchwork step, not in temporal precedence. (b) Causal finitism: modal event-based finitism over momentary states (FiniteDistinctAncestry of a supplied state-causation relation in every accessible history) plus the explicit precedence-to-causation bridge (every earlier state is a causal ancestor of a populated later state) gives the same conclusion (populatedPastsFoundedOfStateFinitism); no no-loops premise is needed because the strict temporal order makes the descent injective. Controls 1 and 2 show both premises are needed: finitism alone is met by causally idle earlier states (an endless past of mere succession survives it), the bridge alone by an endless past in which every earlier state causes every later one. So a holder of H2 must reject the Reaper assembly bridge, and must reject modal state-causal finitism or the precedence-to-causation bridge. H1 replacement account: an initial or sempiternal contingent thing (an initial state of the universe) never preceded by its absence. H1 finding: in a history whose populated pasts are founded, if every contingent concrete thing has an existing concrete ground (STMT-EVERY-CONTINGENT-GROUNDED-AT) and grounds precede what they ground in time (no merely simultaneous grounding), every contingent concrete thing comes to be; with H2 priced, possibleness of such a populated history yields A3′ (possiblyFoundedOfEarlierGrounds, a new non-transcription support option for A3′ reaching STMT-GOD-EXISTS). H1 survives the grounding premise when grounding may be simultaneous: control 4 (a necessary individual sustains a never-generated contingent one on Nat time) and control 5 (two contingent individuals sustain each other; no necessary concrete individual; grounding not well-founded). Control 5 shows the rival who denies a necessary concrete being and keeps every contingent thing grounded under simultaneous grounding must accept non-well-founded grounding, the horn BruteFoundationBoundary.bruteRootOrNonWellFounded already forces; with well-founded grounding the existing theorem gives a brute contingent root instead. Price summary for the initial-state rival who denies a necessary concrete being: H2 costs the Reaper assembly bridge, and modal state-causal finitism or the precedence bridge; H1 costs either a brute (ungrounded) contingent thing, or simultaneous grounding together with non-well-founded (for example circular) grounding. Neither price is called unreasonable here; each is a definite commitment. The rooted control (6) satisfies every new premise and bridge jointly. Nothing is attributed to Koons, Pruss or any source. No premise is established.
blocker: All new premises are OPEN. Next tests: (1) whether the Reaper assembly bridge can be weakened to a patchwork principle about accessible worlds whose content is not already equivalent to founded pasts, and whether the rival's denial of it conflicts with other spine commitments (for example the recombination it uses elsewhere); (2) whether the precedence-to-causation bridge can be weakened to some earlier state per populated moment, and whether an endless past of mere succession conflicts with inert emptiness or A1; (3) for H1, whether a simultaneous ground of a contingent thing can be required to be necessary (connecting to join premise J1), and whether the bounded-past-resource result (BoundedPastResource.noUniformGrowth) gives an independent H2 price under a stock-growth premise.
